title: Nellie Bly's birth chart
metaDescription: Nellie Bly's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 15.4° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 11.5° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 15.4° of Taurus is the Sun's exact seat — second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Mercury in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 5.0° Gemini; Venus stands at 25.6° Aries; Mars stands at 13.5° Pisces. The tradition reads thought that travels by comparison from Mercury, attraction declared rather than implied from Venus, effort that surges when it matters from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Mars a sixth of the circle apart from Pluto, 1.6° off exact. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted. Behind it, the Sun sextile Mars at 1.9°, and Mercury sextile Neptune at 2.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: No closed figure — no grand trine, t-square, or grand cross — holds among the day-stable angles. The chart distributes its tension pair by pair rather than through one standing structure.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, four placements stand out. The Moon in Taurus at 11.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Gemini at 5.0° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Venus in Aries at 25.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Libra at 12.5° is in exaltation. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives earth 3, air 3, fire 2, water 2, and fixed 4, mutable 3, cardinal 3 across the modes. Earth signs hold the scheme’s slow end, where results are measured in what survives rather than what starts. Jupiter and Saturn were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.7° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 11.5°.
